channel.title: Overnight Brief
channel.description: A private daily audio digest of the strongest insights from the overnight newsletters. Built for one listener.

item.title: Ep 69: The Ungovernable Week
item.description: The week Jensen Huang stopped being untouchable: Nvidia's board met Wednesday night on his future after the NYT named Alice Huang, the stock shed two trillion in five weeks, Congress wants a briefing, and Baird cut its target from five hundred to two hundred. Deep dive: CoreWeave's twenty-four percent pop and Michael Intrator's off-contract GPU math - one hundred thirty thousand GPUs re-renting for four billion a year at zero capex, and why the bond market already prices the split. Plus Anthropic's multiple-times-oversubscribed IPO and its toothless Long-Term Benefit Trust, the METR and AI Futures acceleration reports, inference startups buying their own chips, Sequoia's bet on AI holding company Sequence, how Anthropic's Ode prices AI rebuilds, and the delayering euphemism.

item.title: Ep 68: The Anchor Bid
item.description: Anthropic IPO week begins: the deal was fully covered at launch, raising up to ninety point four billion at a one point two six to one point four trillion valuation. Deep dive: Matt Levine's anchor-investor mechanics - why a share of Anthropic is worth more to Google than to you, the twenty-six billion dollar price-insensitive tranche, and the Amazon and Google payoff math. Plus OpenAI's ten billion dollar quarter and the twelve percent valuation gap, The Information's seven point five billion dollar Huang chips-to-China exclusive, Google's search ads faltering, the enterprise token-cap divergence, hot CPI and rate-hike talk, CoreWeave's prepayment pivot, and Nidus' thirty million for defense robotics.

item.title: Ep 67: The Materiality Test
item.description: Day two of the Jensen Huang fallout: Nvidia slides four percent while the rest of the market rips, AMD jumps thirteen percent, and Google unveils new AI chips. Deep dive: Matt Levine's question - is the Nvidia affair securities fraud? The everything-is-securities-fraud machine, materiality, key-man risk, and why a one percent probability shift is worth tens of billions. Plus the export-controls push in the NDAA, the Fireworks hack, Meta's enterprise sales build-out, and three Indian Series As.

item.title: Ep 66: The Absorption Test
item.description: The week the AI trade gets audited: Nvidia's board investigates reports that Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort after he admitted an affair; Anthropic starts its IPO roadshow with a listing the week of November 16 while CoreWeave prints into a fifty percent monthly slide; Deep dive: how Cisco got bullwhipped in 2000 - the virtual supply chain, the double orders, and the two point two billion dollar writedown that maps onto today's neocloud order books. Plus the anti-AI rotation into India, the Unity approach, and the OCC's super intelligence rulebook.

item.title: Ep 65: The Other West Texas
item.description: Two West Texases: The Information's investigation into Musk's real Texas buildout - gigawatt-scale gas at Starbase, a gigawatt of power ships off Brownsville, 800 megawatts at Bastrop, and the air permit now gating 10 gigawatts of promised 2027 capacity. Deep dive: SemiAnalysis tours Galaxy in Inner Mongolia, China's 800-megawatt answer to Stargate Abilene - first phase in under a year at a fifth of US cost, over 60 percent wind-powered, solid-state transformers already live. Plus Noah Smith turns China bear, a Dutch bank quietly sells data-center loans, the weekend's gracious hedging, and Alaska still uncalled.

item.title: Ep 64: The Rebound Test
item.description: Friday happened twice: Asia face-planted into Thursday's hole - Nikkei down 6 percent, Kospi's 8.8 percent circuit breaker, Taiwan in a bear market - then the US bounced 1.1 percent on a hot jobs report. Stripe's cash registers say software is accelerating while stocks say it's dying; the Anthropic IPO whisper slides to 1.2 trillion. Deep dive: TSMC weighs 3D DRAM at Nvidia's request - memory from first principles, the cyclicality trap, and the SK Hynix conflict. Plus Miller as chief of staff, Huang asked to attend a closed-door House briefing on Nov 18, Musk's 400 million dollar Texas backlash and the Cybertruck's end, Fal's 1.65 billion, Unity's 26 billion approach, and the agent cloud stack.

item.title: Ep 63: The Hangover
item.description: The morning after the blue wave: the Nasdaq 100 drops 6.4 percent, wiping out 2.3 trillion dollars, Tesla and SpaceX sink, and the compute narrative flips from shortage to glut. Alaska and Prop 40 still uncalled; Scott Wiener heads to Congress on his opponent's concession. Deep dive: SemiAnalysis benchmarks Google's TPU v7 Ironwood against Nvidia on agentic inference. Anthropic's S-1 tokenomics - roughly 895 billion in headline compute commitments, a third cancellable or unwritten, 4.5 billion on the balance sheet. Plus Nvidia's telecom-building retrofit plan with Apollo, Cyera's 800 million raise at 20 billion, and the Chesky side quest.

item.title: Ep 62: The Blue Wave
item.description: The results are in: Democrats take the House and Senate, Hinojosa flips Texas, Bottoms flips Georgia, Donalds holds Florida, Prop 40 trailing but uncalled, Alaska still counting. What the blue wave does to data centers, AI regulation and big tech margins; prediction markets called it hours early; Anthropic IPO demand is infinite while OpenAI wants a comeback; the Cerebras lockup lesson; and Apollo now owns 75 billion dollars of AI chips.

item.title: Ep 61: The Night So Far
item.description: Election night, no calls yet: only APs Virginia Senate call for Democrats as we record; the uncalled data-center governor map in Texas, Georgia, Florida and Alaska; Salesforce spends 25 billion in cash on eight AI deals; SpaceX revises its 2027 target to 13 GW and builds data centers in months; the Hyperliquid perps pricing Anthropic IPO pop; Claude helps design Anthropic chips; the Binance hackers came in through a fake job interview; and the AI buildout pivots from debt to equity.

item.title: Ep 60: The $900 Billion Question
item.description: Anthropic's amended S-1: $17B in Q3 revenue against $657B of signed compute commitments and nearly $900B of planned spend, as investors talk the IPO down to $1.5T; America votes with data centers and Prop 40 on the ballot; Apple's first Ternus quarter beats then guides down, and the nine-year slog of the J595 robot; the AI debt wave hits credit markets and Marvell's Lumentum math; Binance's very traditional recovery; and the race to make GPU time a traded commodity.

item.title: Ep 59: The Backlash Ballot
item.description: Midterms-eve: data centers are on the ballot in 36 governor races and pause candidates are poised to win up to 15; the 62 GW of 2028 capacity at stake; Apple, Palantir and Uber report into the worst tech tape in a year; the FBI blames North Korea for the Binance heist as withdrawals reopen; OpenAI trims its own fundraise; and why space data centers cost 100x.

item.title: Ep 58: Meet Max
item.description: Meta secretly built a humanoid called Max with China's Fourier - 106 pounds, three months, and already a version two; California votes Tuesday on a one-time billionaire tax and the polls are knife-edge; the Journal probes a $1,000 hands-free driving device after fatal crashes; the real economics of DoorDash buying Instacart; and humans rewriting themselves to sound less like AI.

item.title: Ep 57: Black October
item.description: The week the AI trade cracked: Nasdaq's worst day since June, Intel's worst session ever, and Alphabet's record drop; the $6.3B Binance heist, biggest in crypto history; security's Black October; DeepSeek's $16B state-backed warchest; what Anthropic's S-1 actually says; the pension funds in line for a windfall; a16z's new founder archetypes.

item.description: Alphabet has its worst day ever and Amazon gets punished for a 39% AWS beat: the AI glass turns half empty; Nvidia extends its $170B backstop habit to Nscale and its $45B Anthropic deal; former Sequoia India partners launch Mettle Capital with $350M; DoorDash buys Instacart for $17B, Thrive takes ADT for $7.6B; a two-year-old AI startup bids for Weil Gotshal and its data.

item.title: Ep 55: The Split Screen
item.description: Alphabet: cloud doubles past $30B but search leaks and free cash flow goes negative $9B; Microsoft retires the Copilot seat metric; the AI security spending spree - 37,000 vulnerabilities a month; Amazon builds a 250M-listing shopping-agent play; DeepSeek and Moonshot distill GPT-6 Astra; the 20-month seed-to-A squeeze.

item.description: OpenAI plans to buy Google TPUs hours before Alphabet earnings; Anthropic day two: the 85% margin reality check, the price war that is not working, and the $63B Broadcom SPV; Levine on Musk's merger pay; Anduril wants $120B and Spark's $777M becomes $9B.

item.description: Anthropic files its S-1: $657B of committed compute, five classes of stock, and a November roadshow; Meta, SpaceX and Apollo make it a quarter-trillion Monday; Stripe vs the card giants on agentic shopping; DoorDash circles Instacart; Brazil crashes.

item.description: High Bandwidth Flash explained from first principles and the ghost of Optane; Anthropic's founder voting control before its IPO; TypeSafe's Jev and cheap confident classifiers; how GPU loans hedge rising rates; and a lightning round on Meta, CPU shortages and AI geopolitics.

item.description: Why GPU clouds are graded on goodput and reliability, not chips; Crusoe's Bronze rating beside its $30.9 billion valuation; US VCs touring China for diligence; the AI discount war's hidden bill; Kalshi's margin filing; and who AI amplifies.

item.description: Why the CFTC paused GPU rental futures and what a compute price would need; how usage pricing is turning software incumbents into AI middlemen; the Tata Sons fight over listing; why long rates track Fed expectations; and a lightning round on China, GPT-6, Meta Muse and industrial AI.

item.title: Ep 18: The Token Factory Splits in Two
item.description: How modern AI inference separates prefill, decode and expert routing; Agility Robotics' $2.5 billion public-market option on robot labour; the race to package persistent personal agents; the authority problem when agents recruit coworkers; and the financing clock beneath AI infrastructure.

item.title: Ep 17: The Memory That Arrived Too Early
item.description: Why Intel Optane worked technically and failed as a market; how Nvidia is coordinating power, buildings, memory and workloads; Jane Street-linked data-center debt at an 11.3% yield; the incentives behind IPO pops; and why GTM agents need state rather than better prose.

item.title: Ep 16: When the Customer Is a Machine
item.description: Why software agents are becoming customers and what a bits-perfect transaction stack requires; Kae Capital's 18x partial exit from Nua; how cheap models move value into physical learning systems; AI safety's culture-war problem; India's regional PE deal tape; and defense tech's distribution incentives.

item.title: Ep 15: Anthropic's Half-Trillion-Dollar Power Bill
item.description: Anthropic's potential $1.5 trillion IPO and up to $517 billion of compute commitments; whether AI labs can police themselves; how Engram moves learned memory from HBM to DRAM; Salesforce yielding the interface to general assistants; and the geopolitical and financial fault lines beneath AI infrastructure.

item.title: Ep 14: Ten Thousand Agents and One Broken Lock
item.description: OpenAI's 10,000-agent, 130-billion-token Navier-Stokes run and what it says about recursive self-improvement; the shared skill-update flaw across four leading coding agents; Bridgewater's call to regulate compute giants like systemic banks; the publisher doom loop; and OpenAI's next private round at a possible $1.2 trillion valuation.

item.title: Ep 13: Compute Needs a Down Payment
item.description: The Fed hike meets AI project finance: GPU prepayments, customer-credit spreads and guarantees; Apollo moves private credit into venture-backed hardware; Apple considers M8 Ultra enterprise servers linked by Nvidia NVLink Fusion; Zipline seeks $1 billion at a $20 billion valuation; and why cost of capital per usable token is the metric beneath the boom.

item.title: Ep 12: Count Megawatts, Not Moratoriums
item.description: Why 300-plus local data-centre restrictions translate into only 1,525 MW of actual delay, how behind-the-meter power changes the winners, OpenAI's agentic software factory and the shift from code generation to verification, enterprise zero-data-retention as a model-market weapon, Meta's camera-free Luna glasses, and why AI subscriptions must earn permission to charge.

item.title: Ep 11: The Speed Limit Becomes a Business Model
item.description: Vera Rubin NVL72 and what its 67x headline really means for agentic inference, KV cache, mixture-of-experts routing, total cost and power; AI leaders ask for a speed limit and markets price safety risk; why regulation solves a coordination problem while protecting incumbents; on-device versus data-centre inference; and the $10B Kioxia ADR and $29.6B ByteDance loan show the capital stack following the rack.

item.title: Ep 10: Amodei Pulls the Brake, the Labs Build Their Own Referee, and the Memory Wall Breaks
item.description: Amodei's Saturday essay calls for an industry slowdown and Altman, Musk, and Trump all react within hours; OpenAI's IPO slips to 2027; The Information reveals Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google were already discussing a self-policing standards body; SemiAnalysis reverses the HBM stack race (4-hi wins, Rubin Ultra downgrades to 192GB); Nvidia's filings show three customers at 44% of sales; the $110M Frederick community deal buys the buildout its politics; and two dozen mathematicians formally warn AI could ruin the foundations of maths.

item.title: Ep 9: Pixxel's $100M Weekend, India's Exit Machine Wakes Up, and Robots vs the Treasury Market
item.description: Pixxel closes the largest round in Indian spacetech ($100M, Temasek + Seraphim) while ISRO staff push back on privatization, India's exit machine prints receipts (Kae's 18x on Nua, Circle buying Tazapay for $400M, Kotak's 2x toll road), the WSJ declares America's Great AI Freakout, Bloomberg asks if robots are ruining the Treasury market with high yields here to stay and $6 diesel, the US links Chinese satellite imagery to a deadly Iranian strike ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, sudden wealth syndrome hits tech's new rich, StarCraft is back while Xbox bleeds, and the FSSAI wants warning labels on your snacks.

item.title: Ep 8: The Fed Blinks at $120 Oil, Nvidia's $530B Shadow Balance Sheet, and the Sanity Caucus
item.description: CPI at 3.4% and futures at 85% for the first Fed hike in three years as the Saudi East-West pipeline shuts and Houthis squeeze Bab al-Mandeb, Brent over $104 with $120 calls, SemiAnalysis maps Nvidia's $530B of off-balance-sheet backstops, Schulman and friends debate recursive self-improvement, the sanity caucus pushes back on extinction math, Instinct's own compute crunch makes the news, and Salesforce vs Figma on whether the UI is dead.

item.title: Ep 7: Oracle's Prepayment Machine, the Sandbox Is Leaking, and Crude Tops $109
item.description: Oracle's 30% growth and the $11.4B customer-prepayment engine financing the AI buildout, OpenAI suspending Pro subs on Astra demand, Jacob Coxon's exit going mainstream plus Anthropic's hotel-Wi-Fi hacking report, the leaky sandboxes inside Claude Code/Codex/Cursor, the $7.5T financing stack and Blackstone's bid, Burry shorting the dollar over quantum, and crude topping $109.

item.title: Ep 6: iPhone Duo Day, Anthropic's Extinction Number, and Where a Robot Thinks
item.description: John Ternus unfolds the $1,999 iPhone Duo and throws down the Siri Recap gauntlet, an Anthropic researcher quits with a 10% extinction warning weeks before the IPO roadshow, OpenAI's agents solve a decades-old math problem while pulling up the drawbridge on Adobe and six Chinese labs, SemiAnalysis on where a robot thinks, Lightfield's $47M Tome redemption arc, and Levine's AAA AI catastrophe-bond warning.

item.title: Ep 5: OpenAI Starts a Price War, Data Beat the Architects, and iPhone Fold Day Is Here
item.description: OpenAI cuts Luna prices and takes the model war to Anthropic's IPO math, Dwarkesh's data-vs-architecture study (12x vs 3.7x), Matt Levine on tokenized AMC, iPhone Fold day and Ternus tonight, Hugging Face's robotics push, a Grok Bot built in a month, agent-era code review, Chime buys Stride for $590M, and Brent over $99 after tanker strikes.

item.title: Ep 4: The TPU Goes Outside, Data Centers Call the Shots, and Apple's Foldable Eve
item.description: SemiAnalysis's first third-party TPUv7 Ironwood benchmarks (up to 50% better perf/dollar than B200), the data-center SLA power flip, Apple's foldable eve with Ternus's first keynote tomorrow, G42/ByteDance/Humain statecraft, the yen's breakout, and Claire's OpenClaw-to-Grok-Bot agent migration.

item.title: Special: The Invisible Layer - What Astra Isn't Saying, and the Jobs That Never Show Up

Act 2: the jobs data - The Economist's one-million-jobs case vs Stanford's 19% young-worker gap, codified vs tacit knowledge, and what it all means for India's $315B IT services industry.

item.title: Ep 3: Anthropic Meets the S-1, Oura's Victory Lap, and the Rise of the Robot Retail Investor

item.description: A 30-minute two-host deep dive: 115 Stratechery emails from March to September 2026 distilled into the six themes that mattered - agents ending the bubble debate, compute as an asset class, Anthropic's safety superpower, the end of Apple's Cook era, China's commoditization battle, and the fall of the gatekeepers.
